title: Engineering Probability and Statistics
description: Equips engineers with probability and statistics as tools for measurement, modeling, experimentation, reliability, process improvement, and evidence-based technical decisions.

topics.title: Engineering Data, Uncertainty, and Statistical Thinking
topics.description: Introduce variation, uncertainty, data quality, and the role of probability/statistics in engineering decisions.

children.title: Engineering Variation and Data Context
children.description: Students learn that engineering data are produced by instruments, processes, people, and environments, not abstract spreadsheets.

children.title: Population, sample, observational unit, variable, parameter, and statistic
Common cause variation, special cause variation, measurement variation, and process variation
Engineering specification, tolerance, acceptance criterion, and safety margin
Cross-sectional data, time series data, experimental data, and field data
Measurement, Error, and Data Quality
children.description: The point is to judge whether data are usable before applying formulas.

children.title: Accuracy, precision, bias, resolution, calibration, and traceability
Random error, systematic error, gross error, and drift
Missing data, censored data, rounded data, duplicated records, and outliers
Data provenance, units, metadata, and reproducible calculations
Statistical Thinking for Decisions
children.description: Students connect uncertainty to practical choices about risk, cost, performance, and evidence.

children.title: Descriptive statistics, inferential statistics, predictive modeling, and decision analysis
Practical significance versus statistical significance
Risk, uncertainty, variability, confidence, and tolerance
Decision threshold, false alarm, missed detection, and engineering consequence

topics.title: Probability Axioms, Counting, and Conditional Probability
topics.description: Build probability models from sample spaces, events, counting rules, conditional probability, and independence.

children.title: Probability Axioms and Event Algebra
children.description: This subtopic builds the formal rules for reasoning about uncertain events.

children.title: Sample space, outcome, event, complement, union, intersection, and mutually exclusive events
Kolmogorov axioms, probability measure, finite additivity, and normalization
Venn diagrams, event partitions, and total probability
Reliability event, failure event, demand event, and exceedance event
Counting for Probability Models
children.description: Counting rules let engineers assign probabilities when outcomes are equally likely or combinatorial.

children.title: Multiplication rule, addition rule, permutations, combinations, and multinomial coefficient
Sampling with replacement, sampling without replacement, and ordered versus unordered sampling
Pigeonhole principle and occupancy models
Defect sampling, inspection lots, component selection, and redundancy combinations
Conditional Probability and Bayes' Rule
children.description: The gist is to update probabilities when new evidence arrives.

children.title: Conditional probability, independence, conditional independence, and dependence
Law of total probability and partition of cases
Bayes' theorem, prior probability, likelihood, posterior probability, and base rate
Diagnostic testing, false positive, false negative, sensitivity, specificity, and predictive value

topics.title: Random Variables, Expectation, Variance, and Transformations
topics.description: Represent uncertain quantities as random variables and summarize them with moments and transformations.

children.title: Random Variables and Distribution Functions
children.description: Students learn how to turn uncertain engineering quantities into mathematical objects.

children.title: Discrete random variable, continuous random variable, support, and parameter
Probability mass function, probability density function, and cumulative distribution function
Quantile, percentile, median, mode, and tail probability
Engineering examples: load, strength, demand, defect count, waiting time, and lifetime
Moments and Summary Measures
children.description: The point is to summarize center, spread, and dependence in interpretable units.

children.title: Expected value, variance, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, and skewness
Covariance, correlation, and standardized variable
Linearity of expectation and variance rules
Moment generating function and probability generating function as optional tools
Functions and Transformations of Random Variables
children.description: Engineering models often transform uncertain inputs into uncertain outputs.

children.title: Linear transformation, monotone transformation, and nonlinear transformation
Change-of-variables method and Jacobian idea
Distribution of sums, products, minima, and maxima
Propagation of mean and variance for simple formulas

topics.title: Common Discrete Distributions for Engineering Systems
topics.description: Use discrete distributions to model counts, defects, arrivals, failures, and finite-population sampling.

children.title: Bernoulli, Binomial, and Geometric Models
children.description: These distributions model pass/fail outcomes, repeated trials, and waiting for first success.

children.title: Bernoulli trial, success probability, and binary indicator
Binomial distribution, number of trials, and number of successes
Geometric distribution, memoryless property, and waiting time
Quality inspection, acceptance sampling, on/off components, and repeated tests
Negative Binomial, Hypergeometric, and Multinomial Models
children.description: Students learn distributions for repeated successes, finite lots, and multiple categories.

children.title: Negative binomial distribution and waiting for r successes
Hypergeometric distribution, finite population, and no replacement
Multinomial distribution and category counts
Lot sampling, batch defects, survey categories, and classification outcomes
Poisson Counts and Rare Events
children.description: The Poisson model is a workhorse for counts over time, space, length, or area.

children.title: Poisson distribution, rate parameter, and exposure interval
Poisson approximation to binomial
Independent increments and count process intuition
Defects per meter, failures per hour, arrivals per minute, and accidents per year

topics.title: Common Continuous Distributions and Lifetime Models
topics.description: Use continuous distributions for measurement variation, waiting times, strengths, lifetimes, and extremes.

children.title: Normal and Related Models
children.description: Students learn the central distribution for measurement variation and many aggregate effects.

children.title: Normal distribution, standard normal, z-score, and empirical rule
Central limit connection and measurement noise
Lognormal distribution for positive skewed quantities
t distribution, chi-square distribution, and F distribution for inference
Waiting-Time and Reliability Distributions
children.description: The goal is to model time-to-event and lifetime data in engineering systems.

children.title: Exponential distribution, memoryless property, and constant hazard
Gamma distribution and Erlang waiting time
Weibull distribution, shape parameter, scale parameter, and hazard trend
Mean time to failure, survival function, cumulative hazard, and reliability function
Bounded, Tail, and Extreme-Value Models
children.description: Engineering decisions often depend on limits, extremes, and bounded physical quantities.

children.title: Uniform distribution and beta distribution
Minimum, maximum, order statistic, and extreme-value idea
Gumbel distribution and block maxima context
Wind loads, flood levels, material strength extremes, and tolerance bounds

topics.title: Joint, Marginal, Conditional Distributions, and Dependence
topics.description: Analyze multiple uncertain variables through joint distributions, covariance, correlation, and dependence structure.

children.title: Joint Distributions and Marginals
children.description: This subtopic teaches students to model multiple uncertain quantities at once.

children.title: Joint probability mass function, joint density, and joint CDF
Marginal distribution, conditional distribution, and conditional density
Bivariate normal distribution and covariance matrix
Contingency table, two-way counts, and joint empirical distribution
Dependence, Covariance, and Correlation
children.description: Students learn to distinguish independence from correlation and to quantify dependence carefully.

children.title: Independence, conditional independence, covariance, correlation, and rank correlation
Positive dependence, negative dependence, and nonlinear association
Correlation is not causation and spurious correlation
Scatterplot, covariance matrix, and pairwise dependence diagnostics
Conditional Expectation and Prediction
children.description: The point is to use known information to predict or reduce uncertainty.

children.title: Conditional expectation, conditional variance, and prediction function
Law of total expectation and law of total variance
Best linear predictor intuition
Engineering examples with sensor readings, loads, weather, demand, and quality indicators

topics.title: Sampling Distributions, Limit Theorems, and Simulation
topics.description: Connect sample statistics to population parameters using sampling distributions, LLN, CLT, and simulation.

children.title: Samples and Sampling Variability
children.description: Students learn why repeated samples produce different estimates.

children.title: Random sample, independent and identically distributed assumption, and sampling frame
Sample mean, sample variance, sample proportion, and sample quantile
Standard error and sampling distribution
Bias, variability, representativeness, and sample size
Law of Large Numbers and Central Limit Theorem
children.description: These limit theorems explain why averages stabilize and why normal approximations appear.

children.title: Weak law of large numbers and convergence in probability
Central limit theorem and normal approximation
Continuity correction and approximation conditions
Engineering interpretation for repeated measurements, simulation outputs, and process averages
Simulation for Sampling Distributions
children.description: Simulation helps students see abstract sampling concepts before relying on formulas.

children.title: Pseudo-random number, random seed, replication, and Monte Carlo experiment
Histogram of simulated statistics and empirical standard error
Simulation error, number of replications, and reproducibility
Bootstrap preview and resampling intuition

topics.title: Point Estimation and Confidence Intervals
topics.description: Estimate parameters and quantify uncertainty using unbiasedness, standard error, confidence intervals, and bootstrap ideas.

children.title: Point Estimators and Estimator Quality
children.description: Students learn that an estimate is a rule with performance properties.

children.title: Estimator, estimate, bias, variance, mean squared error, and consistency
Method of moments and maximum likelihood estimation
Standard error and plug-in estimate
Estimator choice for mean, variance, proportion, rate, and reliability parameter
Confidence Intervals for Common Parameters
children.description: The point is to report uncertainty around estimates, not just point values.

children.title: Confidence level, margin of error, critical value, and degrees of freedom
z interval, t interval, proportion interval, variance interval, and rate interval
One-sample, paired, and two-sample intervals
Engineering interpretation of confidence interval versus coverage
Bootstrap and Practical Interval Issues
children.description: Students learn flexible interval ideas and common mistakes in interpretation.

children.title: Percentile bootstrap, bootstrap standard error, and resampling with replacement
Small sample, nonnormal data, skewness, and robustness
Confidence interval versus prediction interval versus tolerance interval
Assumption check, sample size planning, and reporting precision

topics.title: Hypothesis Testing, Statistical Power, and Engineering Decisions
topics.description: Test claims while interpreting Type I/II error, p-values, effect size, practical significance, and power.

children.title: Hypothesis Test Logic
children.description: This subtopic builds the decision framework used in engineering evidence claims.

children.title: Null hypothesis, alternative hypothesis, test statistic, rejection region, and p-value
One-sided test, two-sided test, significance level, and critical value
Type I error, Type II error, and error consequence
Practical significance, effect size, and engineering threshold
Common Parametric and Nonparametric Tests
children.description: Students learn a toolkit for comparing means, proportions, variances, and distributions.

children.title: One-sample t test, two-sample t test, paired t test, and z test
Chi-square goodness-of-fit test and chi-square test of independence
F test, ANOVA preview, and variance comparison
Wilcoxon, Mann-Whitney, sign test, and permutation test intuition
Power and Sample Size
children.description: The goal is to design tests that can detect meaningful engineering differences.

children.title: Power, minimum detectable effect, sample size, and variability
Operating characteristic curve and acceptance sampling link
Multiple testing, false discovery, and familywise error
Decision risk, cost of sampling, and cost of wrong conclusion

topics.title: Correlation, Regression, Prediction, and Model Diagnostics
topics.description: Model relationships among engineering variables using simple/multiple regression, prediction intervals, and diagnostics.

children.title: Simple Linear Regression
children.description: Students learn to model a response as a function of one predictor and quantify uncertainty.

children.title: Response variable, predictor variable, slope, intercept, and residual
Least squares, fitted value, residual sum of squares, and R-squared
Standard error of slope, confidence interval, and hypothesis test for slope
Calibration curve, material property relationship, and process trend example
Multiple Regression and Prediction
children.description: Engineering systems often require several predictors and careful prediction intervals.

children.title: Multiple linear regression, adjusted R-squared, interaction term, and polynomial term
Prediction interval, confidence interval for mean response, and extrapolation risk
Categorical predictor, indicator variable, and model hierarchy
Collinearity, variance inflation, and feature scaling
Diagnostics and Model Adequacy
children.description: The point is to detect when a regression model is misleading.

children.title: Residual plot, normal probability plot, leverage, and influence
Outlier, high-leverage point, Cook's distance, and studentized residual
Heteroscedasticity, nonlinearity, autocorrelation, and omitted variable
Transformation, weighted least squares, and validation split

topics.title: Design of Experiments and Response Surface Methods
topics.description: Plan efficient experiments using randomization, replication, blocking, factorial designs, ANOVA, and response surfaces.

children.title: Experiment Planning Principles
children.description: Students learn to generate strong evidence efficiently instead of collecting convenient data.

children.title: Experimental unit, factor, level, response, treatment, and nuisance variable
Randomization, replication, blocking, and control
Confounding, aliasing, lurking variable, and bias
Completely randomized design, randomized block design, and paired design
Factorial Designs and ANOVA
children.description: This subtopic teaches students to estimate main effects and interactions.

children.title: Full factorial design, fractional factorial design, main effect, and interaction
Two-level design, design matrix, contrast, and effect estimate
ANOVA table, sum of squares, mean square, F statistic, and p-value
Residual analysis, multiple comparisons, and practical interpretation
Response Surfaces and Optimization
children.description: The goal is to use statistics to improve engineering performance.

children.title: Response surface method, first-order model, second-order model, and curvature
Central composite design, Box-Behnken design, and contour plot
Steepest ascent, desirability function, and robust parameter design
Process optimization, sensitivity, and confirmation run

topics.title: Statistical Quality Control, Capability, and Process Monitoring
topics.description: Use statistical methods to monitor, improve, and control engineering processes.

children.title: Control Charts for Variables and Attributes
children.description: Students learn to separate routine variation from signals that require action.

children.title: Shewhart chart, center line, control limit, and rational subgroup
x-bar chart, R chart, s chart, individuals chart, and moving range chart
p chart, np chart, c chart, and u chart
Western Electric rules, run rule, false alarm, and special cause
Process Capability and Specifications
children.description: The point is to compare process variation with engineering tolerances.

children.title: Specification limit, control limit, tolerance, and target value
Cp, Cpk, Pp, Ppk, and sigma level
Capability for normal and nonnormal data
Defects per million opportunities and yield
Quality Improvement and Acceptance Sampling
children.description: Students connect statistics to manufacturing and operational decisions.

children.title: Acceptance sampling, producer's risk, consumer's risk, AQL, and LTPD
Operating characteristic curve and average outgoing quality
Pareto chart, cause-and-effect diagram, and process improvement cycle
Measurement system analysis, repeatability, reproducibility, and gauge R&R

topics.title: Reliability, Failure Probability, Risk, and Availability
topics.description: Model failure behavior, reliability, hazard, maintainability, redundancy, and risk metrics.

children.title: Reliability and Lifetime Functions
children.description: This subtopic introduces the probability language of dependable systems.

children.title: Reliability function, survival function, CDF, PDF, and failure probability
Hazard function, bathtub curve, mean time to failure, and mean residual life
Censored data, right censoring, and life-test dataset
Exponential, Weibull, lognormal, and gamma lifetime models
System Reliability and Redundancy
children.description: Students learn how component reliability combines into system reliability.

children.title: Series system, parallel system, k-out-of-n system, and standby redundancy
Reliability block diagram and fault tree
Common-cause failure, independence assumption, and load sharing
Availability, maintainability, repair rate, and mean time to repair
Risk Metrics and Engineering Safety
children.description: The goal is to connect probability estimates to risk-informed decisions.

children.title: Failure probability, reliability index, consequence, expected loss, and risk matrix
Factor of safety versus probability of failure
Sensitivity of risk to distribution choice and tail behavior
Civil, industrial, electrical, and mechanical engineering reliability examples

topics.title: Uncertainty Propagation, Monte Carlo, and Technical Communication
topics.description: Propagate uncertainty through engineering models and communicate probabilistic results for decisions.

children.title: Uncertainty Propagation in Models and Measurements
children.description: Students learn how uncertain inputs produce uncertain outputs.

children.title: Measurement uncertainty, model uncertainty, parameter uncertainty, and aleatory/epistemic uncertainty
First-order Taylor approximation and delta method
Root-sum-square propagation and sensitivity coefficient
Calibration uncertainty, instrument uncertainty, and uncertainty budget
Monte Carlo Simulation and Variance Reduction
children.description: Simulation supports complex engineering models when closed-form formulas are impractical.

children.title: Monte Carlo simulation, input distribution, model response, and output distribution
Random seed, convergence, simulation standard error, and number of trials
Latin hypercube sampling, antithetic variates, and control variates
Scenario analysis, sensitivity analysis, tornado chart, and percentile estimate
Communicating Uncertainty for Decisions
children.description: The final skill is to present uncertainty clearly enough to support action.

children.title: Executive summary, assumptions, uncertainty interval, and decision recommendation
Visualization: histogram, boxplot, density plot, prediction band, and error bar
Risk statement, caveat, limitation, and sensitivity result
Reproducible report, documented code, and traceable calculation
